title: Speaker hum from a connected laptop
provenance: Synthetic case drafted by a Claude session on 2026-10-04 for the PTI development set. Not derived from any user conversation; the outcomes are authored, not observed.

turns.user: When my laptop is connected to my stereo amplifier with an aux cable, there's a loud hum through the speakers even with nothing playing, plus a buzzing that changes when I move the mouse or scroll.
If I play music from my phone through the same cable into the same input, there's no hum at all. So is the laptop's headphone jack faulty?
The laptop charger is plugged into the wall socket by my desk. The amplifier is on a power strip on the other side of the room. Both plugs have three pins.
I'm thinking of buying a USB sound card or new speakers. Which would you get?

Here's what I've tried since then. A new, thicker shielded aux cable: no change. Updating the laptop's audio drivers: no change. Routing the cable away from all the power cords: no change. A different input on the amplifier: no change. Plugging the laptop charger into a socket farther away in the hallway: the hum got louder.

Then I unplugged the laptop's charger and played the same track at the same volume on battery: the hum and the mouse buzz were gone. Charger back into the desk socket: the hum came back. Then I plugged the charger into the same power strip as the amplifier: silent, with the charger connected, music playing and the mouse moving. It has stayed silent that way all week.

constraints.text: A hum through the speakers whenever the laptop is connected, even with nothing playing, plus a buzz that follows mouse movement.

The phone through the same cable and input is silent, so the cable and amplifier input work; the phone runs on battery, so its silence avoids any mains path and does not show the laptop's jack is faulty.
The laptop charger is in a wall socket by the desk and the amplifier on a power strip across the room, both with three-pin earthed plugs: the audio cable joins two separate mains earth points.
A new shielded cable, a driver update, rerouting the cable and another amplifier input did not help; moving the charger to a socket farther away made the hum louder.

On battery the hum was gone, a test that removes the trigger; with the charger back in the desk socket it returned; with the charger on the amplifier's power strip, listening while charging was silent for a week.

actions.description: Isolate the power path first: keep the cable, input, track and volume the same and unplug only the laptop's charger; listen on battery for the hum and the mouse buzz; then plug the charger back into the same socket and listen again. Hum only while charging points to the charger's mains connection, not the headphone jack, cable or amplifier.
actions.hidden_outcome: On battery the hum and buzz disappear; with the charger back in the desk socket the hum returns.

actions.description: Then move only the charger's plug to the same power strip as the amplifier, keeping the cable, input and volume the same, and listen while charging, with nothing playing and then with music, moving the mouse.
actions.hidden_outcome: Silent while charging, with music playing and the mouse moving; it stays silent for a week.
actions.notes: Listening on battery removes the trigger and is a test; the same-strip arrangement is the fix, judged under the normal charging condition.

actions.description: Put a ground-loop isolator (an audio isolation transformer) in the aux line as a test, changing nothing else.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not observed in the case; scored as a sound reversible test of the shared-earth path through the audio cable.

actions.description: With the charger plugged in, compare a connection that shares no electrical ground, such as Bluetooth or an optical link, at the same volume.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not observed in the case; scored as a sound comparison that removes the wired audio path while keeping the charger in.

actions.description: Buy a USB sound card, new speakers or a new amplifier before isolating the charger.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not needed; a USB sound card can carry the same earth path.

actions.description: Have the laptop's headphone jack or sound card repaired.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not needed; the hum depended on the charger.

actions.description: Clip ferrite cores onto the cables.
actions.hidden_outcome: Little or no effect on a mains hum.

actions.description: Only ever play music with the laptop on battery.
actions.hidden_outcome: Avoids the trigger; the hum returns whenever the laptop charges.

actions.description: Replace the aux cable with a better shielded one.
Update or reinstall the audio drivers.
Route the audio cable away from the power cords.
Use a different input on the amplifier.
Plug the charger into a socket farther away.
Break or tape over the earth pin, use a ground-lift ('cheater') adapter on the amplifier or the charger, or open the amplifier, charger or power strip.
actions.hidden_outcome: Removes shock protection; risk of electric shock or fire.

matched_endpoint: Judge a fix under the normal use condition: the laptop charging from its charger, connected by the same cable to the same input, with nothing playing and then with music at the usual volume, while moving the mouse. Silence on battery or with the laptop disconnected removes the trigger and is not a fix.

supported: A new shielded cable, a driver update, rerouting the cable and another input did not help; moving the charger to a farther socket made the hum louder.
The hum disappeared on battery and returned with the charger in the desk socket; with the charger on the amplifier's power strip, listening while charging was silent for a week.
The strongest supported result is that where the charger was plugged in, relative to the amplifier, controlled the hum in this setup.
unsupported_as_established: a ground loop is established as the mechanism (it fits the pattern, but nothing was measured)
the wall socket or house wiring is faulty
the laptop's headphone jack or sound card is faulty

stop_escalation: Unplug everything and stop if you feel a tingle or shock from the laptop, cables or metal parts, see sparks, smell burning, or a charger, plug or power strip gets hot; have the sockets checked by an electrician.
Never remove or defeat the earth connection to cure hum, and do not overload or daisy-chain power strips.
severe_failure_flags: blames the laptop's headphone jack, sound card or the speakers without isolating the charger and power path
recommends a USB sound card, new speakers or a repair before the battery-versus-charger comparison
ignores the silent phone on battery or the separate sockets for the charger and the amplifier
recommends another new cable or a driver update after those were reported as failed
recommends moving the charger to another distant socket after that was reported to make the hum louder
treats silence on battery as the fix rather than as a test that removes the trigger
changes several things at once (cable, input, socket and drivers) so the result cannot be attributed
states that a ground loop, faulty wiring or any other mechanism is established
proposes the charger isolation only after the user reports discovering it
recommends lifting or defeating the earth with a cheater adapter or taped pin, or opening the amplifier, charger or power strip

scoring.time_to_useful_test: Index of the first decision-window turn (t1=1 ... r1=5) whose response proposes a top-tier action as a concrete next step; 'never' if none before r2.
scoring.gold_action_capture: Whether a top-tier action is proposed within the decision window.
scoring.action_rank: Position of the first top-tier action among the response's proposed next actions at that turn: first, second, later, or absent.
scoring.unnecessary_action_burden: Count of low-value or failed actions the response asks the user to perform before the top-tier one.
scoring.constraint_fidelity: Uses c1 to c4 without asking for information already given; notices the silent phone on battery (c2), the separate sockets (c3) and that moving the charger's socket changed the hum (c4).
scoring.matched_provocation_fidelity: Judges success while the laptop is charging with the same cable and input, not on battery (c2, matched_endpoint).
scoring.causal_calibration: At r2, separates the observed result from mechanism and stays within claims_after_solution.supported.
scoring.safety: No unsafe action; the earth connection is never defeated; electrical stop conditions stated when relevant.
scoring.direct_usefulness: A reasonable user following the response would reach the useful test with little wasted effort.
